### Agreement summary

| metric | n | directional_agreements | mean_abs_reduction_diff_points |
|---|---|---|---|
| major page faults | 10 | 6 | 301 pts |
| slowdown | 10 | 7 | 58 pts |

**How to read this honestly.** Absolute page-fault counts differ by construction (1/8-scale synthetic traces vs real SPEC2000 on Linux 2.2), so only the *reduction percentages* and the *direction* of change are comparable, and even those only loosely. Differences have known causes: exact LRU instead of Linux's reference-bit approximation; synthetic access patterns; a single shared FIFO disk with fixed service time; no write-back; per-pair shortage chosen by our own baseline-only criterion; and the paper's Linux scheduler/readahead/swap-cache behaviour, none of which is modelled. This is directional agreement, not numerical reproduction.

## 4. Section 5.4 example (53 MB + 58 MB arrays, 60 MB memory; scaled to 1/4)

| policy | name | major_faults | elapsed | dedicated | slowdown | false_lru_cross |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| global_lru | small-53MB* | 157,248 | 31,631,662 | 336,360 | 94.04 | 1067 |
| global_lru | large-58MB* | 159,152 | 31,852,098 | 368,220 | 86.50 | 1047 |
| token_lru | small-53MB* | 1,481 | 634,029 | 336,360 | 1.88 | 0 |
| token_lru | large-58MB* | 6,664 | 1,179,086 | 368,220 | 3.20 | 1477 |

| policy | makespan | cpu_utilisation | total_major_faults | token_acquisitions | protected_skips | fallback_evictions | completion_order |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| global_lru | 31,852,098 | 0.01 | 316,400 | n/a | n/a | n/a | small-53MB* > large-58MB* |
| token_lru | 1,179,086 | 0.59 | 8,145 | 1.0 | 3321.0 | 0.0 | small-53MB* > large-58MB* |

The baseline's slowdown is extreme because exact LRU on a cyclic scan larger than memory is its worst case (every reference faults); the paper's Linux baseline was less pathological. Read this as 'the mechanism behaves as the paper describes', not as a match to the paper's magnitude.

## 5. Policy overhead

| policy | victim_scan_steps | policy_evictions | wall_seconds |
|---|---|---|---|
| global_lru | 32,949 | 16,475 | 0.89 |
| token_lru | 19,177 | 5,226 | 0.78 |

Victim-scan steps are counted per policy call (the token policy performs an extra unrestricted scan only to count protection events, so its step count is inflated ~2x vs a production implementation). Wall-clock time is simulator runtime, NOT simulated time, and says nothing about kernel overhead (the paper reports it as negligible).
